appraisal_events.evidence: « Tu sais, avait dit Mme Verdurin à son mari, je crois que nous faisons fausse route quand par modestie nous déprécions ce que nous offrons au docteur... il s'en rapporte à ce que nous lui en disons. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme Verdurin's blunt calculation that Cottard cannot judge the real value of things, offered as a rationale for cheapening what they give him, exposes a petty, exploitative side beneath her professed regard for him.

appraisal_events.evidence: au lieu d'envoyer au docteur Cottard un rubis de trois mille francs... M. Verdurin acheta pour trois cents francs une pierre reconstituée en laissant entendre qu'on pouvait difficilement en voir d'aussi belle.
appraisal_events.explanation: M. Verdurin's quiet execution of the swap - a cheap imitation stone passed off as rare and fine - portrays him as stingy and duplicitous, independent of what it reveals about Cottard.

status_effects.explanation: Her frank rationale for cheapening gifts to Cottard, dressed up as pragmatism, casts her locally as calculating and self-serving.
His execution of the deceptive substitution, feigning generosity while giving something cheap, locally marks him as stingy and duplicitous.

ambiguities: The narrator reports the Verdurins' scheme mostly without explicit editorializing; whether this constitutes a distinct local diminishment of the Verdurins themselves, versus simply serving as evidence for Cottard's gullibility (already captured in the accepted annotation), is a matter of interpretation.
